We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So it's a bis-aryl sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl to a phenyl with a cinnamamide (trans). The target has two aromatic amine groups: one is the sulfonamide linking to tolyl (para methyl phenyl). The other is an anilide (amide) attached to phenyl with an amino group (para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an amine at para? Wait Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with two amino groups? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an amine at position 1 and another amine at position? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amine attached to the aromatic carbon (the N attached to aromatic carbon) and also an amine substituent on the aromatic ring? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the aromatic carbon is attached to N (the amide N) and also the ring has an N substituent at the other end (an aniline). So it's a diamino phenyl (para-aminophenyl). So the amide is attached to a 1-aminophenyl (para-aminophenyl). So the product is a sulfonamide linking to a phenyl that has a trans-cinnamamide attached to a para-aminophenyl.

We need to find commercially available precursors. Likely we can disconnect at the sulfonamide bond (S-N) and at the amide bond (C-N). So retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide: target -> sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the other aromatic with sulfonamide). Actually the sulfonyl part is attached to the tolyl ring (para methyl). So we can use p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) reacting with the aniline (the other aromatic containing the amide). So precursor A: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). Precursor B: 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamido)phenylamine? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to the aniline (the phenyl with the amide). So the aniline is 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamido)aniline? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the aniline at the para position relative to the amide? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the tolyl ring (with methyl) has sulfonamide attached at para position (relative to methyl). The sulfonyl group attaches to the other phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) at para position relative to the side chain (the cinnamamide). So the second phenyl is para-substituted with sulfonyl group and the side chain (cinnamamide). So the aniline after sulfonylation is 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamido)aniline (i.e., 4-aminophenyl with amide attached to another 4-aminophenyl). Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: that's an amide linking to a 4-aminophenyl (para-aminophenyl). So the second phenyl (c2) has the side chain at para position (the side chain attaches via the double bond to carbonyl to an aniline). So the second phenyl is 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamido)aniline? Wait the side chain attaches via the double bond to the carbonyl attached to N of aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to a 4-aminophenyl. So the side chain is trans-cinnamoyl attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the second phenyl (c2) is a phenyl bearing sulfonyl group (para) and the side chain (para). Actually both substituents are para to each other? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. This phenyl has the side chain at position 1 (attached to aromatic carbon). The sulfonyl attaches to that phenyl via S(=O)(=O) attached to N of sulfonamide, not directly to aromatic carbon. So the phenyl is attached to sulfonyl via N (the sulfonamide N attaches to phenyl). So the phenyl is part of sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the phenyl is attached to sulfonyl via the sulfonyl nitrogen. So the phenyl is the sulfonyl aryl group (p-tolyl). Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the tolyl ring (the first phenyl). Actually NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2: the sulfonyl nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (first phenyl) and the sulfonyl S is attached to the second phenyl (c2). So the sulfonyl group is bridging the two phenyls: one side attached to N (connected to tolyl), other side attached to aromatic carbon (c2). So the sulfonyl is aryl sulfonyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we can think of using 4-methylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) reacting with the aniline (the second phenyl) which is 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamido)aniline (i.e., an aniline with a para-cinnamamide substituent). So step 1: sulfonylation.

Step 2: Disconnection of amide: the aniline (para-aminophenyl) attached via amide to cinnamoyl. So we can use 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Actually the amide is formed from cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) and 4-aminophenyl. The side chain is trans-cinnamoyl (CH=CH-CO-) attached to N of aniline. So we can make the amide by coupling 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) with trans-cinnamic acid (or its acid chloride). So precursor: 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine? Actually we need a phenyl with an amine at para position, and also the other para position is free for sulfonylation later. So the aniline we need is 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine) but one amine will be used for amide formation, the other for sulfonylation later. So we can start from p-phenylenediamine (commercial). Then we can protect one amine (e.g., as Boc) to allow selective acylation. But we have only 3 steps total. We could do sequential functionalization without protection if we use selective reagents: e.g., first acylate one amine with trans-cinnamoyl chloride under conditions that preferentially acylate the less hindered amine? Both are similar. Might need protection. But we have 3 steps max, so we could protect one amine (Boc), then acylate, then deprotect and sulfonylate. That's 3 steps (protect, acylate, sulfonylate). However we also need to attach the tolyl sulfonyl group; that is step after deprotection. So total steps: 1) protect one amine of p-phenylenediamine (e.g., Boc2O). 2) acylate the free amine with trans-cinnamic acid chloride (or using coupling reagent). 3) deprotect (remove Boc) and sulfonylate with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride. That's 3 steps (if deprotection and sulfonylation can be combined? Probably separate). That would be 4 steps. Need max 3 steps. Alternative: start from 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) already having the amide formed (i.e., trans-cinnamoyl aniline) commercially? Maybe trans-cinnamoyl aniline (cinnamoylaniline) is commercially available. Let's check. Use search_catalog_by_smiles for "O=C(C=C)Nc1ccc(N)cc1".
